cards.title: Oscilloscope in the web page with an on/off button
cards.description: A 440 Hz sine wave generated by the Rust engine (WASM in an AudioWorklet), played in the web page with an on/off button and shown live on an oscilloscope.

cards.title: DSP foundations: state-of-the-art audio quality before more boxes
cards.description: Set the audio quality bar before writing many boxes: objective measurements, deterministic denormals, smoothed parameters with sample-accurate events, an allocation-free audio thread in the browser, and benchmarks.

tasks.title: Engine design decisions, recorded before any code that depends on them: messages, event scheduling, feedback, polyphony, multichannel, rates, parallelism, hot swap, latency, state; including the Nyquist policy of oscillators, an exact integer phase accumulator, the output stage (headroom, non-finite samples), the input domain of boxes, and compiling, instantiating, parsing and building plans off the audio thread, or bounding and measuring what must stay there (the construction of the engine processor), hot swap included

Objective measurements in engine-testkit and the oracle: spectrum, THD, SNR, aliasing level, with thresholds per box; spur and aliasing laws across the rate matrix; the banned float methods audited against the toolchain
Deterministic strategy for denormal numbers, proven on every target: a subnormal conformance case, and a native test with flush-to-zero forced on
Typed, smoothed parameters (kinds such as frequency, with a declared Nyquist policy) and sample-accurate timestamped events, in the engine and the patch format

Allocation-free audio thread in the browser, without per-frame garbage: oscilloscope through an AnalyserNode; capture and metering through a SharedArrayBuffer ring when cross-origin isolated, with a tested fallback otherwise; garbage collections while rendering measured in every browser engine, not only in V8
Benchmarks in CI: instruction counts per box and for building large plans, with regression thresholds; the construction of the engine processor timed on the three browser engines

cards.title: Integration engine: plugin contract to import other patch formats
cards.description: Start the integration engine: a small, documented plugin contract (detect, import) that turns a foreign patch file into our patch format plus an import report (each source object converted, approximated or unsupported, never silently lost). Integrations are pure, treat their input as untrusted, and their output is validated by the engine's own patch reader. Every registered integration is tested automatically by a shared test kit. Depends on the patch format (#3) and on the message model (#12).

cards.title: Music notation foundations: a first engraved score in a responsive box
cards.description: Lay the foundations of music notation like the DSP foundations do for audio: design decisions first, then the smallest complete vertical slice, a proof of concept of the whole chain. The first case is the D Dorian scale in quarter notes on one treble-clef staff, engraved by a Rust library and shown in a fully responsive box of the web page. The library depends on no platform: layout produces a display list (positioned glyphs and lines) that is identical on every target, and thin renderers draw it. Quality is proven like the audio engine: laws, a conformance case, an independent oracle. Note events keep their symbolic information, decided with the engine design (#12).

tasks.title: Design decisions recorded before any code: score data model (spelled pitches, exact rational durations, voices, stable element ids; inspired by the MNX draft), layout units (integer fractions of a staff space), display list format and its canonical hash, crate layout, SMuFL font and its metadata, how the layout fits a given width, licenses of every dependency checked
Score model, the minimum for the first case: one staff, treble clef, 4/4, spelled pitches in quarter notes, exact rational durations, validated at the boundary

Layout as a pure function of the score and a width: staff, clef, time signature, note heads, stems and their direction, bar lines and final bar line, justified on one line; laws over the width matrix: deterministic, no collision, notes on the right staff positions
Command line and first conformance case, the D Dorian scale in quarter notes: SVG render and canonical hash of the display list, reference render reviewed by an engraver
WebAssembly bindings: the same display list hash as native, proven by end-to-end tests in the browsers and in Node

Web page: the score drawn with Canvas 2D in a fully responsive box (phone to wide screen, every pixel density, laid out again on resize, always one line), with a text description for screen readers; end-to-end and accessibility tests on Chrome, Firefox and WebKit
Independent oracle (TypeScript): rereads the SVG, recomputes the hash and checks the laws and the expected notes, in cargo xtask check
Deep review: every finding analyzed and applied, then a fresh review

cards.title: Declare the supported browsers
cards.description: Name the oldest version of each browser the playground, the editor and the documentation site support, and check the code against that baseline (a lint of the web APIs used, or a build target), so that an older browser always gets the explanation of what it lacks, never a TypeError. Until then, newer APIs are banned one by one by the shared lint configuration.
